guide: Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the target hours to a first reply, the days a quote stays valid, the most due dates you take in a month and the income per hour you want from a package.
Check Packages, Pay rates, Areas, Sources and Team. They hold the prices, the hours, the mileage rates and the phones that the other sheets look up. A solo doula keeps one doula and no backup.

Write every enquiry in Enquiries: date, name, phone, area, service, the due date wanted (a date the enquirer gives, used only to plan the on-call window: the days around it when a doula keeps themselves free), source and first reply.
Book each consultation in Consultations and check the Consultation Calendar for free slots. Record the minutes, the outcome and the follow-up date.
Build each quote in the Quote Builder, then write it in Quotes. A deposit is a payment that reserves the date and is applied to the price; the balance is the rest of the price after the deposit.
Read the Follow-up List every morning: it tells you who to call, write to, remind or welcome today.
Use Demand by Due Month before you say yes to a date: it shows the clients booked and the open quotes against the most due dates you take in a month.
Read Funnel by Month, Source Conversion, Reply Time Bands and Lost Reasons each month to see where enquiries drop out and which sources sign.
Use the 18 tools to build a quote, check the funnel, rank the lost-enquiry causes, test a discount, forecast the next 30 days and find the weekday that needs reply cover.
Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.

Replace the demo data: clear the yellow rows of each sheet and type your own. Everything calculated fills in again by itself. The workbook has no macros and works in Excel and other spreadsheet tools.
Read the Enquiry Dashboard and the Charts sheet every week: enquiries, replies, consultations, quotes, contracts, lost enquiries and demand by due month.

listing.title: Doula Business Enquiries, Consultations and Quotes Excel Template: Quote Builder, Funnel, Lost Enquiries, Due-Month Demand
listing.headline: Win more clients: from the first enquiry to a signed quote
listing.description:
Run the front door of a doula business in one Excel workbook. Built for an owner-doula, a small doula agency or a solo doula who answers enquiries, holds consultations, sends quotes and decides which due dates to accept.

Enquiries records every enquiry with the source, the service and the due date wanted, the hours to a first reply and the outcome. Consultations and the Consultation Calendar show booked, held and missed consultations and the free slots. Quotes holds the package, the discount, the add-ons, the travel fee, the deposit, the balance date, the instalment dates and the valid-until date, and the Follow-up List tells you who to call, write to or welcome today.

Funnel by Month, Source Conversion, Reply Time Bands, Lost Reasons and Lost Value by Month show where enquiries drop out and which sources sign. Demand by Due Month sets the enquiries and open quotes wanting each month against your own monthly limit before you say yes to a date.

18 tools answer the weekly questions: a quote builder with income per hour against your target, a funnel check, a lost-enquiry cause analyser, a due-month demand map, a 30-day pipeline forecast, reply-time impact, a discount cost test, quote expiry, package win rates, a travel fee check and instalment offers. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to enquirers, clients, the owner-doula, the admin, a doula and a care-provider office.

This is part one of the Doula Business suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, with a demo copy full of sample data to explore first. Clients appear by name, area, due date and package only, with no medical detail. It helps you keep track of dates, hours, money and capacity and does not promise results. Prices and targets are your own settings. Check your local rules for contracts, privacy and records.
